profile.name: AIM Academy
profile.mission: Grow the academy Faster, Stronger, and even Better to positively impact the development of youth in our community and create a lifelong passion for the sport.
profile.vision: Develop opportunities in sport by providing a professional environment where all can reach their full potential.
profile.figuresNote: Figures as reported in the AIM catalogue (2025), not live figures: 20 activities, 70 employees (2 PWD), 1,000+ members, 12+ coach trainings/certifications, 500 trees planted.

activationDate.note: Not stated in the catalogue — enter when confirmed.

coreValues.note: The catalogue mentions 5 core values but does not list them — enter when confirmed.

questions.prompt: In which year was AIM Academy established?
questions.explanation: About Us: “Established in 2021, our journey began as a soccer academy…”

questions.prompt: What do the letters A-I-M stand for?
choices: Assess – Identify – Master
Aspire – Inspire – Motivate
Assess – Improve – Mentor
Achieve – Inspire – Master
questions.explanation: The AIM logo reads “Assess • Identify • Master”.

questions.prompt: AIM’s journey began as which kind of academy?
choices: A soccer academy
A multi-sport youth academy
A music and arts academy
An after-school education centre
questions.explanation: About Us: “our journey began as a soccer academy”. Other disciplines came later under the Faster pillar.

questions.prompt: Which statement most accurately reflects AIM’s vision?
choices: To develop opportunities in sport through a professional environment where everyone can reach their full potential.
To diversify academy activities while expanding youth participation across disciplines.
To strengthen coaching standards and provide structured development opportunities for young athletes.
To build a sustainable academy through partnerships, certified training, and community engagement.
questions.explanation: Vision: “Develop opportunities in sport by providing a professional environment where all can reach their full potential.” The other options describe the pillars or the board’s growth model.

questions.prompt: AIM’s mission is to grow the academy Faster, Stronger and even Better to positively impact youth development in the community — and to do what else?
choices: Create a lifelong passion for the sport
Produce professional players for national clubs
Build a network of certified coaches across Lebanon
Give every child access to a professional environment
questions.explanation: Mission: “…to positively impact the development of youth in our community and create a lifelong passion for the sport.” The last option echoes the vision, not the mission.

questions.prompt: What best describes the difference between AIM’s mission and its vision?
choices: The mission says how AIM grows (Faster, Stronger, Better) to impact youth; the vision describes the opportunities and environment AIM provides
The mission focuses on coaches and staff; the vision focuses on members and their families who join AIM
The mission covers community projects; the vision covers sports results and competition success
The mission is about education programs; the vision is about sport and physical activity only
questions.explanation: Mission = grow Faster, Stronger, Better to impact youth and create lifelong passion. Vision = develop opportunities in sport through a professional environment where all can reach their potential.

questions.prompt: Who is AIM’s Founder & CEO?
choices: Nabil El Fakih
Wael Shehayeb
Ali Abdel Khalek
Sami Baz
questions.explanation: Nabil El Fakih is Founder & CEO. The others are AIM board members.

questions.prompt: Besides leading AIM, which corporate role does the catalogue list for the CEO?
choices: PepsiCo GTM Modernization Sr. Manager – AMESA & APAC
PepsiCo Regional Sales Director – Levant
Coca-Cola Commercial Excellence Manager – MENA
Unilever Supply Chain Lead – AMESA
questions.explanation: The CEO profile lists “PepsiCo GTM Modernization, Sr. Manager – AMESA & APAC”.

questions.prompt: Which two community roles does the catalogue list for the CEO?
choices: Vice president of Akhaa Ahli Aley and vice president of Oxygen NGO
President of Jabal Sporting Club and board member of Farah Social Foundation
Executive committee member of the Lebanese Football Association and of Go Green
Founder of Heroes Initiative and of Yalla Return
questions.explanation: CEO profile: Akhaa Ahli Aley vice president; Oxygen NGO vice president. The second option describes board member Ali Abdel Khalek.

questions.prompt: In his message, the CEO says AIM is shaping not just athletes, but…
choices: future leaders who will make a meaningful impact in their communities
certified coaches who will lead the next generation of academies
professional players ready for national and international teams
community volunteers who will support local NGOs and clubs
questions.explanation: Message from the CEO: “we are shaping not just athletes, but future leaders who will make a meaningful impact in their communities and beyond.”

questions.prompt: According to the CEO, AIM’s pillars aim to inspire a lifelong passion for what?
choices: Both sport and education
Sport and healthy living
Sport and community service
Music, arts and sport
questions.explanation: “…we strive to foster youth development and inspire a lifelong passion for both sport and education.”

questions.prompt: According to the board members, which elements make up AIM’s sustainable growth model?
choices: Training, tournaments, partnerships, value-added services and community impact
Membership fees, sponsorships, events, merchandise and coaching
Training, scholarships, competitions, media and volunteering
Coaching, facilities, partnerships, fundraising and outreach
questions.explanation: Board message: “a sustainable model focused on training, tournaments, partnerships, value-added services, and community impact”.

questions.prompt: Which AIM board member is a member of the Lebanese Football Association’s executive committee?
choices: Wael Shehayeb
Ali Abdel Khalek
Sami Baz
Nabil El Fakih
questions.explanation: Wael Shehayeb: member of the executive committee, Lebanese Football Association. Ali Abdel Khalek presides over Jabal Sporting Club; Sami Baz heads AIM’s legal department.

questions.prompt: The catalogue reports 1,000+ members, 20 activities and 70 employees. If membership doubled, which pillar’s work would matter most for keeping coaching quality high?
choices: Stronger
Faster
Better
AIM Forward
questions.explanation: Stronger covers professional training and coach certification “to upscale the capability of our team” plus curriculum and methodology — exactly what protects coaching quality during growth.

questions.prompt: AIM reports 12+ professional trainings and coach certifications. What purpose does the catalogue give for them?
choices: To upscale the capability of AIM’s team
To qualify coaches for national federations
To meet ministry licensing requirements
To prepare members for competitions
questions.explanation: Stronger pillar: “12+ professional trainings/certified our coaches to upscale the capability of our team while also building a skilled curriculum & methodology”.

questions.prompt: For the past three years, AIM has focused on its 3 pillars and what else to define and drive its culture?
choices: 5 core values
4 community projects
12 coaching standards
3 strategic partnerships
questions.explanation: Catalogue: “Over the past three years we have focused on our 3 Pillars & 5 core values to define and drive our culture.” (The five values are not listed in the catalogue.)

questions.prompt: AIM wants one new project that serves the Better pillar most directly. Which proposal fits best?
choices: Partnering with a local NGO on a recurring community clean-up and awareness day
Adding fencing and robotics to the list of weekly activities
Running a new certification course for AIM’s gymnastics coaches
Upgrading the mobile app with online class booking
questions.explanation: Better = community engagement (p.7). New disciplines belong to Faster; coach certification to Stronger; the app is an operational tool.

questions.prompt: A proposal adds three new disciplines (photography, swimming and coding). Which pillar does it primarily advance?
choices: Faster
Stronger
Better
AIM Forward
questions.explanation: Faster is the pillar of diversification: AIM “evolved to offer a diverse range of over 20 activities under our faster pillar”.

questions.prompt: Match each program to its primary objective.
options: Empower individuals with special needs to master their talents
Offer specialized vocational training courses with expert trainers
Support learning through afterschool, French and Brainy programs
questions.explanation: Heroes (p.8), Green Influence (p.9), Education (p.10), AIM Forward (p.11).

questions.prompt: Match each partner or group to its part in AIM’s community work.
options: Ran recycling awareness sessions with AIM
Promoted recycling under the slogan “Trash for cash”
Event where the Ahlaa Alam team took part
questions.explanation: Go Green Recycle and Yalla Return partner with Green Influence (p.9); the Ahlaa Alam team (Heroes) took part in the AUB Able Summit (p.8); members supported Plant a Tree (p.9).

questions.prompt: How does the catalogue list each organization: MOU partner or collaboration?
questions.explanation: AIM Profile page: MOUs include Beirut Marathon Association, Farah Social Foundation and Fayha; collaborations include PepsiCo, Institut Français and the Municipality of Aley.

questions.prompt: Sort each item into the catalogue section where it appears.
questions.explanation: Camps (p.14), activities (p.12), Heroes (p.8), Green Influence (p.9), AIM Forward (p.11).

questions.prompt: What does AIM do each week as part of the Heroes Initiative?
choices: Hosts a different organization to join AIM’s activities
Runs an adaptive-sports clinic for partner schools
Holds a talent showcase for families and sponsors
Trains volunteers to support members with special needs
questions.explanation: Heroes Initiative: “Each week, we host a different organization to participate in our activities.”

questions.prompt: In which seasons does AIM run camps?
choices: Winter, spring and summer
Summer only
Spring and summer
Summer and winter
questions.explanation: Catalogue: “Winter, Spring, Summer Camps”.

questions.prompt: How many of AIM’s 70 employees does the catalogue identify as persons with disabilities (PWD)?
questions.explanation: AIM Profile: “70 employees (2 PWD)”.

questions.prompt: The Faster pillar’s list of activities includes one program that the catalogue also presents as a community program. Which one?
choices: Heroes Initiative
Green Influence
AIM Forward
Plant a Tree
questions.explanation: The Faster pillar lists “…gymnastics, Heroes Initiative, kickboxing…” (p.7); Heroes is also a community engagement program (p.8).

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of Green Influence’s home pickup service?
choices: To encourage sorting waste at the source
To collect donated sports equipment from members
To deliver reusable bags to new member families
To gather recyclables for the Trash for cash program
questions.explanation: “We introduced a home pickup service to encourage sorting waste at the source.”

questions.prompt: How did AIM further support waste sorting beyond the pickup service?
choices: Distributed bins and reusable bags at no cost
Sold discounted recycling bins at the AIM Center
Installed sorting stations in partner schools
Offered membership discounts for recycled items
questions.explanation: “We distributed bins and reusable bags at no cost, making a measurable impact on the environment.”

questions.prompt: Which programs does the catalogue group under Education?
choices: Afterschool, French and Brainy
Chess, Rubik’s Cube and Brainy
Afterschool, French and Chess
French, Piano and Choir
questions.explanation: Education: “Afterschool, French, Brainy”.

questions.prompt: How does AIM Forward develop its vocational training courses?
choices: With affiliate institutions and recognized expert trainers
With AIM’s certified coaches and in-house curriculum
With online courses licensed from universities
With volunteers from the Heroes Initiative
questions.explanation: “We leverage our robust network of affiliate institutions and collaborate with expert trainers…”

questions.prompt: Which of these is listed among AIM’s Faster-pillar activities?
choices: Arm-wrestling
Swimming
Tennis
Basketball
questions.explanation: The Faster pillar lists after-school program, arm-wrestling, arts and crafts, brainy kids, chess, calisthenics, choir, French, gymnastics, Heroes Initiative, kickboxing, Rubik’s cube, self-defense, summer camp, dance and music.

questions.prompt: AIM wants to strengthen inclusion next season. Which step builds most directly on the existing Heroes Initiative?
choices: Invite more partner organizations into the weekly sessions and assess each participant’s talents
Launch a new robotics class that is open to all members
Certify two more gymnastics coaches for competitive squads
Add a winter camp option for older members
questions.explanation: Heroes Initiative assesses unique talents of individuals with special needs and hosts a different organization each week (p.8).

questions.prompt: Which new idea extends Green Influence most consistently with what AIM already does?
choices: Expand the home pickup service and awareness sessions to more neighbourhoods
Add an outdoor fitness class in public parks
Host a recycling-themed chess tournament for members
Offer vocational courses in sports management
questions.explanation: Green Influence already runs awareness sessions and a home pickup service (p.9); scaling these is the most consistent extension.

questions.prompt: A senior coach proposes a “coach mentoring” track for new coaches. Which pillar does it most directly strengthen?
choices: Stronger
Faster
Better
Education
questions.explanation: Stronger = professional training, coach certification and curriculum to upscale the team’s capability (p.7).

questions.prompt: AIM wants to help young adults gain job-ready skills. Which existing initiative is the natural home?
choices: AIM Forward
Heroes Initiative
Green Influence
After-school program
questions.explanation: AIM Forward develops “specialized professional training courses” — vocational training (p.11).

questions.prompt: Which launch plan best reflects the board’s sustainable growth model for a new sports program?
choices: A training plan, a tournament calendar, a partner organization and a community element
A premium membership tier, branded kit and a social-media campaign
A single sponsor, a free trial month and a referral discount
External coaches, a short pilot term and a parent survey
questions.explanation: The board describes growth through training, tournaments, partnerships, value-added services and community impact (p.5).

questions.prompt: Reconstruct AIM’s three pillars. Which mapping is correct?
clues: The pillar numbered 01 is the one under which AIM grew to over 20 activities.
The pillar numbered 02 is about certifying coaches and building a curriculum.
The pillar numbered 03 is focused on community engagement projects.
In catalogue order, the pillars are named Faster, Stronger, Better.
choices: Faster – activity diversification · Stronger – coach training & curriculum · Better – community engagement
Faster – coach training & curriculum · Stronger – activity diversification · Better – community engagement
Faster – activity diversification · Stronger – community engagement · Better – coach training & curriculum
Faster – community engagement · Stronger – coach training & curriculum · Better – activity diversification
questions.explanation: Pillars 01 Faster (20+ activities), 02 Stronger (12+ trainings, curriculum), 03 Better (community engagement).

questions.prompt: Open the Culture Lock: a 3-digit code.
clues: Digit 1 = the number of pillars that guide AIM’s culture.
Digit 2 = the number of core values the catalogue says AIM focuses on.
Digit 3 = the number of community projects AIM launched under the Better pillar.
Check: the three digits add up to 12.
questions.explanation: 3 pillars, 5 core values, 4 Better projects → 354 (3+5+4 = 12).

questions.prompt: Open the Green Vault: a 4-digit code.
clues: Digit 1 = the number of trees AIM and its members planted, divided by 100.
Digit 2 = the last digit of the year AIM was established.
Digit 3 = the number of seasons in which AIM runs camps.
Digit 4 = digit 1 minus digit 3.
questions.explanation: 500 trees → 5; established 2021 → 1; winter, spring, summer camps → 3; 5 − 3 = 2 → 5132.

questions.prompt: AIM by the numbers: what is A + B + C + D?
clues: A = the number of activities on the AIM Profile page.
B = the number of AIM employees.
C = how many of those employees are persons with disabilities (PWD).
D = the minimum number of professional trainings/certifications for coaches. (Member numbers are not part of this sum.)
questions.explanation: 20 activities + 70 employees + 2 PWD + 12 trainings = 104.

questions.prompt: Crack the Season Code: four letters.
clues: Letters 1–3 are the first letters of the seasons in which AIM runs camps, in the catalogue’s order.
The catalogue lists the camps starting with the coldest season.
Letter 4 is the first letter of the language class listed under Education.
The code contains no vowels.
choices: WSSF
SSWF
WSSE
SWSF
questions.explanation: Winter, Spring, Summer camps (p.14) → W-S-S; French under Education (p.10) → F.

questions.prompt: Unlock AIM’s mission statement. Combine your fragments: which version is exact?
clues: It begins: “Grow the academy…”
It includes: “…Faster, Stronger, and even Better…”
It includes: “…to positively impact the development of youth in our community…”
It ends: “…and create a lifelong passion for the sport.”
choices: Grow the academy Faster, Stronger, and even Better to positively impact the development of youth in our community and create a lifelong passion for the sport.
Grow the academy Faster, Stronger, and even Better to provide a professional environment where all youth in our community can reach their full potential.
Grow the academy Faster, Stronger, and Better to positively impact the development of our members and create a lifelong passion for sport and education.
Develop the academy Faster, Stronger, and even Better to positively impact youth in our community and build future leaders through sport.
questions.explanation: Mission (p.3): “Grow the academy Faster, Stronger, and even Better to positively impact the development of youth in our community and create a lifelong passion for the sport.”

questions.prompt: A talented child dominates every activity, while less experienced children are losing confidence. What is the most effective coaching approach?
choices: Give the talented child leadership roles (demonstrating, mentoring) and use rotating roles and mixed-ability groups so everyone gets meaningful involvement
Move the talented child to an older, more advanced group so the current group can play at its own level
Introduce a rule limiting how often any one child can score or lead, and explain it to the whole group
Keep the current setup because competition motivates everyone, and give quieter children extra drills after class
questions.explanation: The strongest response develops everyone: the talented child is stretched through leadership while others gain involvement — AIM’s vision of all reaching their full potential.
questions.source: Hypothetical scenario (grounded in AIM vision, catalogue p.3)

questions.prompt: A parent is visibly upset after the final whistle because their child did not play in the tournament final. What should the coach do?
choices: Acknowledge the frustration, arrange a private conversation once emotions settle, explain the participation approach and agree a development plan
Refer the parent to academy management to avoid a coach–parent conflict
Explain the decision immediately at the pitch side so the parent hears the reasoning
Reassure the parent that the child will start the next match to ease the tension
questions.explanation: Calm, private, transparent communication with a plan for the child builds trust; promises about selection undermine fairness.
questions.source: Hypothetical scenario (grounded in AIM vision, catalogue p.3)

questions.prompt: A child with special needs joins a mixed group. Some children become impatient when drills slow down. What is the best approach?
choices: Adapt the activity so everyone can take part, assign buddy roles, and talk with the group about respecting different abilities
Run a separate adapted station with an assistant coach for the first few weeks, then integrate gradually
Ask the parents what works best for their child before changing anything in the session
Keep the session unchanged and let the child join in where possible, to avoid singling them out
questions.explanation: This reflects the Heroes Initiative spirit (p.8): adapt so everyone participates and build a culture that values every ability.
questions.source: Hypothetical scenario (grounded in AIM vision, catalogue p.3)

questions.prompt: Two children keep arguing during team drills and blaming each other for mistakes. What should the coach do?
choices: Pause, speak with both calmly, help them say what happened, agree a team rule, then pair them in a cooperative task
Put them on different teams for the rest of the term to keep the peace
Give both a short time-out and restart the drill
Let the team captain sort it out, since peers resolve conflicts best
questions.explanation: Resolving the conflict and rebuilding cooperation teaches a life skill; separation or time-outs only pause the problem.
questions.source: Hypothetical scenario (grounded in AIM vision, catalogue p.3)

questions.prompt: A 9-year-old has lost several chess games in a row and now wants to quit. What is the most effective response?
choices: Ask what they enjoy, set small personal goals (like learning a new opening), celebrate progress over results, and pair them with a similar-level peer
Enter the child in an easier tournament so they can win and regain confidence
Suggest they try a different AIM activity that might suit them better
Encourage them to keep going, explaining that resilience comes from losing
questions.explanation: AIM’s mission is a lifelong passion: focusing on personal progress keeps motivation intrinsic.
questions.source: Hypothetical scenario (grounded in AIM vision, catalogue p.3)

questions.prompt: During camp, a coach notices a child has unexplained bruises and has become unusually withdrawn. What should the coach do?
choices: Follow the academy’s child-protection procedure: record observations factually and report to the designated safeguarding lead the same day, without investigating
Gently ask the child what happened and record their full account in detail
Contact the parents directly to ask about the bruises before escalating
Watch the child closely over the next few sessions before reporting anything

rubric.label: Reports promptly through the right channel

questions.explanation: Safeguarding best practice: report concerns promptly to the designated lead; coaches should not investigate or alert possible sources of harm.
questions.source: Hypothetical scenario (grounded in AIM vision, catalogue p.3)

questions.prompt: Twenty children want to join a tournament that only has 12 places. How should places be decided?
choices: Use selection criteria shared in advance (attendance, effort, development) and offer the others a friendly match or alternative event
Draw names at random so selection is purely luck-based
Select the 12 strongest players to give the team its best chance
Let the children vote on who should go
questions.explanation: Transparent criteria plus a meaningful alternative keeps it fair and developmental.
questions.source: Hypothetical scenario (grounded in AIM vision, catalogue p.3)

questions.prompt: A parent offers a coach paid private sessions, hinting this should help their child get selected for the competitive team. What should the coach do?
choices: Decline any link between private payment and selection, explain selection follows academy criteria, and inform management
Accept the private sessions but state clearly they will not affect selection
Decline politely without telling anyone, to avoid embarrassing the parent
Refer the parent to another coach for private sessions
questions.explanation: Selection must stay independent of payments; informing management protects the coach, the child and fairness.
questions.source: Hypothetical scenario (grounded in AIM vision, catalogue p.3)

questions.prompt: A shy child in ballet freezes before her first performance. What should the coach do?
choices: Acknowledge her nerves, rehearse a short part privately, start her in a group section, and praise her effort
Ask a parent to stand nearby during the performance for reassurance
Let her skip this performance and watch from backstage
Place her in the front row so she gets used to the spotlight quickly
questions.explanation: Gradual, supported exposure builds lasting confidence.
questions.source: Hypothetical scenario (grounded in AIM vision, catalogue p.3)

questions.prompt: In the after-school program, a child shows exceptional drawing talent but is struggling academically. The parents want a homework-only focus. What is the best approach?
choices: Meet the parents, share specific observations, propose homework support plus a short weekly arts slot, and review progress together
Follow the parents’ wish and keep the child on homework only
Suggest the parents look for an external art school
Enrol the child in arts and crafts sessions anyway, since talent should be nurtured
questions.explanation: AIM = Assess, Identify, Master: identify the talent and build a balanced plan with the family.
questions.source: Hypothetical scenario (grounded in AIM vision, catalogue p.3)

questions.prompt: TEAM DISCUSSION — agree as a team. Your U10 soccer team lost 8–0 and some players blame the goalkeeper. What is your team’s agreed post-match approach?
choices: Huddle, acknowledge effort, name two things that went well and one to improve, and state clearly that the team wins and loses together
Skip discussion today and address it at the next training once emotions have calmed
Speak privately with the goalkeeper to reassure them, then move on
Review each goal conceded straight away while it is still fresh
questions.explanation: Collective responsibility protects individuals and builds team culture.
questions.source: Hypothetical scenario (grounded in AIM vision, catalogue p.3)

questions.prompt: TEAM DISCUSSION — agree as a team. AIM is invited to a high-profile tournament (top players only) and a Heroes Initiative community event (all members) on the same weekend. Coaches are split. What does your team recommend?
choices: Split resources: send a smaller squad to the tournament and involve all other members and coaches in the Heroes event, explaining the plan to families
Choose the community event, since inclusion is central to AIM
Choose the tournament for visibility and promote the community event online
Let families decide by survey which event AIM supports
questions.explanation: The board’s model combines tournaments and community impact (p.5); the vision is about opportunities for all (p.3).
questions.source: Hypothetical scenario (grounded in AIM vision, catalogue p.3)

questions.prompt: TEAM DISCUSSION — agree as a team. A parent criticises a coach in the class WhatsApp group in front of other parents. What should AIM do?
choices: Reply briefly in the group that you will call them directly, then discuss privately and follow up with a short written summary
Ask management to remove the message and contact the parent
Reply in the group with a full explanation so all parents hear the facts
Ignore it in the group and wait for the parent to contact the academy
questions.explanation: Acknowledge publicly, resolve privately, and document the follow-up.
questions.source: Hypothetical scenario (grounded in AIM vision, catalogue p.3)

questions.prompt: The choir and dance coaches disagree over rehearsal time for a joint showcase. What is the best way forward?
choices: Meet together, map both groups’ needs, agree a shared schedule and create one joint piece that blends both groups
Split the rehearsal time equally and keep the two groups separate
Ask management to decide the schedule
Give priority to whichever group performs first
questions.explanation: Coaches modelling collaboration shows members what teamwork looks like.
questions.source: Hypothetical scenario (grounded in AIM vision, catalogue p.3)
